sections.heading: 4. Days 22–30 and Reviews at 60/90: Kill Weak Plays, Fix Bottlenecks, Scale Evidence
paragraphs: Use Days 22–30 to consolidate evidence rather than expand the advertising surface. On Day 22, refresh buyer specifications; on Day 23, test asking prices against recent comparable transactions where obtainable, distinguishing realized sales from auction estimates and advertised prices. On Day 24, resolve inspection defects and revised freight costs. On Day 25, have the document contractor audit lien and settlement packets. On Day 26, calculate contribution for each active proposal. On Day 27, reconcile paid and committed spending. On Day 28, test alert accuracy and duplicate suppression. On Day 29, prepare the decision packet; on Day 30, assign Kill, Fix, or Scale to each tested play and to the overall sprint. Report untested plays separately instead of declaring them successful or unsuccessful. The packet includes unique counterparties, verified assets, qualified buyers, confirmed matches, written proposals, actual fees collected, projected contribution, and owner hours. An active proposal requires a buyer-confirmed next event within fourteen days. Remove stale proposals from active counts until the buyer reconfirms. Zero Day 30 revenue is compatible with the canonical 2–9 month first-deal window; zero usable authority or demand is a different problem.

Apply decision rules in order: Kill overrides Fix, and Scale requires every listed condition for that checkpoint. Kill means stop new spending on the affected play, withdraw unreliable listings, and preserve records; it does not mean abandon existing contractual duties. A missed review-date burn ceiling freezes all new discretionary spending until commitments and cash are reconciled. Confirmed seller impersonation, fabricated ownership evidence, or an unresolved mandatory authorization also stops the affected activity immediately. For commercial testing, count only personalized attempts to relevant named counterparties, not bulk impressions. At Day 30, stop a tested play with forty seller approaches and zero verified assets, or thirty buyer approaches and zero qualified buyers. Otherwise, a shortfall against Scale thresholds receives one fourteen-day repair plan with one owner, one bottleneck, and a measurable target. Examples include securing two missing mandates, converting three qualified interviews into one confirmed match, or correcting delivered costs on two proposals. Do not solve documentary failure with more advertising. At later checkpoints, use the cumulative activity thresholds below and the dated repair record to distinguish an unproven market from a repeatedly failed execution process.

Scale at Day 30 means reallocating up to 20% of existing prospecting hours toward the strongest play, with no headcount increase and no budget increase. Day 60 Scale adds at most 25% more alert volume within the same four-person pod, provided the listed evidence and capacity tests pass. Day 90 Scale allows a separately budgeted expansion proposal, not automatic adoption of the $800,000 annual case. Define a late critical task as a scheduled authority check, inspection report, payoff confirmation, or settlement action more than two business days overdue. Keep this count at zero before scaling. For pipeline coverage, multiply each active proposal's expected commission by a conservative 20% planning weight and sum the results; require at least $9,000 of weighted commissions at Day 90. This is a liquidity stress proxy, not booked revenue or an empirically established close probability. Maintain at least three active proposals across three unrelated buyers and three separate assets, and preserve the $7,500 reserve. No closing by Day 90 triggers Fix rather than automatic Kill when demand remains credible. Authorize the additional full-time person and fourth contractor only through a new capacity and cash plan supported by collected fees and repeatable work.

Calculate direct-cost contribution for every proposal and total commitments
Keep cumulative paid and committed spending within $7,500
Retain opportunity cost sheets and obligation-inclusive cash ledger
Day 28: Owner tests matching accuracy and duplicate suppression
Audit twenty alerts or all alerts when fewer exist
Repair mismatched specifications before increasing buyer notification volume
Retain audit results with zero unresolved duplicate opportunities
Days 29–30: Owner prepares packet and assigns decisions
Classify every tested play using priority-ordered checkpoint thresholds
Publish one decision, accountable owner and dated next action
Retain separate untested-play list and signed Day 30 review
Day 30 Kill: Affected play stops new discretionary spending
Forty seller approaches yield zero assets; or thirty buyer approaches yield zero qualified buyers
Stop tested play; enterprise spending also freezes above $7,500
Retain contact logs, verification failures and contractual closeout responsibilities
Day 30 Fix: Surviving play misses any Scale requirement
No Kill trigger exists but one Scale threshold fails
Assign one fourteen-day repair with no added spending authorization
Retain named bottleneck, numeric target and Day 44 review
Day 30 Scale: Enterprise meets every listed readiness condition
Four verified assets, twelve qualified buyers, four matches, two proposals; spending at most $7,500
Reallocate up to twenty percent of existing prospecting hours
Require positive contribution on both proposals and zero late critical tasks
Day 60 Kill: Tested play remains commercially nonfunctional
Eighty seller approaches yield fewer than two assets; or sixty buyer approaches yield zero matches
Stop affected play; enterprise spending also freezes above $12,000
Retain cumulative unique contact counts and prior repair outcomes
Day 60 Fix: Surviving operation lacks complete Scale evidence
No Kill trigger exists but any Scale condition remains unmet
Run one fourteen-day repair without increasing the monthly ceiling
Retain owner-specific action plan and scheduled Day 74 review
Day 60 Scale: Enterprise demonstrates advancing executable demand
Six verified assets, eighteen qualified buyers, six matches, three active proposals; spending at most $12,000
Increase alert volume at most twenty five percent within pod
Require two scheduled buyer inspections, positive proposal contribution and zero late critical tasks
Day 90 Kill: Tested play fails repeated demand repair
Eighty qualified-counterparty approaches, two completed repairs, and zero active proposals jointly trigger exit
Stop affected play; enterprise spending also freezes above $16,500
Retain repair histories; hard authority or fraud failures override timing
Day 90 Fix: Credible pipeline lacks expansion readiness
No Kill trigger exists but any Scale condition remains unmet
Maintain current pod; zero closings alone does not compel exit
Rebudget runway before further commitments and schedule Day 104 review
Day 90 Scale: Enterprise supports a separately budgeted expansion proposal
Eight verified assets, twenty four buyers, eight matches, three active proposals, $9,000 weighted fees
Require spending at most $16,500 and reserve at least $7,500
Require three unrelated buyers, three assets, positive contributions and zero late critical tasks

chapters.pull_quote: Scale verified authority and executable buyer demand before you scale listings, headcount, or confidence.
action_checklist: Map P1–P7 in one CRM, choose one primary asset lane and one adjacent lane, and assign one primary play to each opportunity.
Confirm the $24,000 sprint funding assumption, cap Day 30 spending at $7,500, and include unpaid commitments in the ledger.
Assign the owner, independent inspector, document coordinator and logistics contractor written responsibilities with capped scopes.
Build four verified asset packets by Day 14, including seller authority, serial evidence, condition disclosures and documented lien-resolution status.
By Day 30, target twelve qualified buyers, four confirmed matches and two positive-contribution proposals while rehearsing independent escrow settlement.
Apply the priority-ordered Day 30/60/90 matrix, record fourteen-day repair targets, and authorize staffing expansion only through a separate funded plan.

statutory_citations.title: UCC Sections 9-301, 9-307 and 9-503 — Governing Law, Debtor Location and Debtor Name
statutory_citations.relevance: Use the applicable state's enacted Article 9 to identify the correct search jurisdiction and debtor name; Sections 9-307 and 9-503 supply related location and naming rules. Certificate-of-title and other exceptions require separate analysis.

statutory_citations.title: UCC Section 9-315 — Secured Party's Rights on Disposition of Collateral
statutory_citations.relevance: A sale does not automatically remove an existing security interest. Establish the applicable exception or secured-party authorization and document release mechanics.

statutory_citations.title: UCC Section 9-513 — Termination Statement
statutory_citations.relevance: Distinguish termination of a financing statement from release of one asset under a continuing secured facility; apply the relevant state enactment.

statutory_citations.title: UCC Section 2-313 — Express Warranties by Affirmation, Promise, Description or Sample
statutory_citations.relevance: Equipment descriptions and factual promises can affect seller warranty obligations. Keep inspection observations, seller representations and untested functions distinct.

statutory_citations.title: UCC Section 2-316 — Exclusion or Modification of Warranties
statutory_citations.relevance: Structure condition disclosures and any warranty exclusions under the applicable state enactment rather than assuming a casual as-is label resolves every issue.

statutory_citations.title: California Vehicle Code Section 11700 — Dealer Licensing Requirement
statutory_citations.relevance: For California fleet activities, determine whether the business falls within regulated dealer activity and obtain required licensing before engaging in it.

statutory_citations.title: 15 CFR 736.2 — Export Administration Regulations General Prohibitions
statutory_citations.relevance: Evaluate jurisdiction, classification, destination, end user and end use before committing to cross-border equipment shipment or related restricted conduct.

statutory_citations.title: 15 CFR Part 744 — End-Use and End-User Controls
statutory_citations.relevance: Review applicable restricted end uses, end users and license requirements; industrial equipment is not exempt merely because it has ordinary civilian uses.
